name: Advanced Grant Writing Patterns
description: This module describes advanced patterns for grant writing intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.
content:
This module describes advanced patterns for grant writing intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When grant writing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. Keep grant writing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. Validate grant writing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
4. When multiple grant writing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
5. Measure before optimizing any grant writing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
6. When grant writing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen grant writing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. Before starting grant writing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
9. Prefer the simplest grant writing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
10. Check that grant writing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting grant writing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of grant writing correctness.
- Avoid introducing new grant writing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for grant writing, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
